title: Stabilize egress probe handoffs on Dedicated nodes to stop transient tenant DNS rebinds
creator: Asha Malik
description:
Summary: Several Dedicated customers reported transient resolution of private hostnames to the wrong tenant during brief node reschedules and GPU pool drains. Symptoms match a short window (1-30s) where egress probe or resolver bindings are reassigned due to multi-path ECMP handoffs and our egress-prober logic performing a 'best-effort' rebinding under reschedule. Impact: cross-tenant DNS resolution and sporadic connection failures for stateful services (databases, metadata endpoints) on Dedicated clusters. Root cause hypothesis: when the dedicated node is drained (evict or GPU pool resize), connections are moved and our probe agent tears down resolver affinity state; concurrently the node-level BPF/eBPF program reorders egress paths and SNAT allocation; resolver probe retries create a competing binding that is accepted by a different tenant's SNAT mapping for a narrow timing window. Key contributing factors: (1) probe timeouts are short and cause aggressive rebind, (2) conntrack reuse across ephemeral port pools for resumed sockets, (3) egress path multipath rebalancing on ECMP-enabled fabric, (4) lack of a reservation handshake between probe agent and node-level SNAT allocator. Goal: implement a low-risk, fast-follow fix that prevents transient cross-tenant DNS rebinding and a safer long-term fix to harden egress affinity. This ticket covers the immediate mitigation, rollout, test, and monitoring.

Reproduction notes: reproducible on a Dedicated cluster with two tenant VPCs sharing the same egress nodes and ECMP enabled. Repro steps summarized: 1) Start long-lived service on tenant A that performs outbound DNS to private resolver. 2) Trigger GPU pool drain on node where tenant A workload runs. 3) Observe egress probe agent on node perform quick rebind; within 1-5s DNS responses can be returned from resolver snapshot tied to tenant B's SNAT port mapping. We reproduced internally with a controlled traffic generator and saw ~12% probability per drain event.

Acceptance criteria: 1) No cross-tenant DNS resolution observed during controlled node drains (zero incidents in 1000 drain trials), 2) No meaningful latency regression for normal outbound flows (<5% p95 change), 3) Feature flag rollout and telemetry available for rapid rollback.
remediation_steps: Add standoff delay in probe agent: on node drain, defer probe rebind until conntrack entries for existing flows age out or a 3s grace window passes.
Introduce short-lived SNAT reservation token between probe agent and SNAT allocator to prevent port reuse for in-flight probe sessions.
Disable aggressive multi-path egress rebalancing while node is in 'draining' state via a node flag exported to routing controller.
Add a fallback to use resolver affinity TTL extension when the tenant has private-resolver metadata set.
Ship as a gated feature-flagged rollout with kill-switch in control plane and circuit-breaker metrics.
test_plan: Unit tests for probe-agent delay logic and SNAT reservation handshake mock.
Integration test: controlled drain harness that exercises 1000 simulated drains across ECMP paths and verifies no cross-tenant DNS mapping.
Canary in staging: enable flag for 10 Dedicated nodes serving low-risk tenants for 72 hours, gather telemetry.
Production rollout: gradual flag increment (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with 30-minute observation windows and auto-rollback on error thresholds.
monitoring: New metric: egress_probe_rebind_events{outcome="mismatch"} counting probe events that resulted in tenant mismatch.
Low-latency alert: if mismatches > 1 in 30m at canary stage, auto-disable flag and page oncall.
Dashboard: dedicated/egress/affinity with time-series of drain events, probe rebinds, conntrack churn, and SNAT port exhaustion.
Post-deploy PoC probe: synthetic tenant-to-resolver pings that assert stable source mapping across drain events.
comments: 2025-01-29 - Asha Malik: Triage call with SRE and Dedicated account owners. Customer A (FinSaaS) escalated with production impact during scheduled maintenance windows.
2025-01-31 - Diego Ramirez: Root cause sketched; conntrack + SNAT reservation race looks plausible. Drafted handshake protocol between probe agent and allocator.
2025-02-03 - Eng Sync: Agreed short-term mitigation = probe delay + SNAT reservation token. Long-term: rework path rebalancer to respect node drain state.
2025-02-06 - PR created: runtime#4822 implements probe-agent delay and feature flag. Initial e2e tests pass in CI but staging canary scheduled.
2025-02-10 - Staging canary (10 nodes) ran for 48 hours; saw 0 mismatches in 120 drain trials. No p95 latency regression observed. Increasing canary to 50 nodes.
2025-02-12 - Diego Ramirez: Rolling to production at 1% with guarded auto-rollback; oncall notified and runbook updated (link in comments).
runbook: On alert: disable egress-probe feature flag globally from control plane UI.
If customers report incidents after rollout: collect packet traces, conntrack snapshots and SNAT allocation lists and attach to ticket.
If auto-rollback triggers: coordinate with SRE to pause scaling events until rollback completes.
Postmortem: require timeline within 3 working days and assign actions for permanent fix in follow-up epic.
postmortem_actions: Create epic to rework egress multi-path rebalancer to be drain-aware (follow-up ticket) - target runtime-1.21.
Audit SNAT port pool sizing and per-tenant segregation options for Dedicated customers (security review required).
Add e2e chaos tests for node drain scenarios in CI harness.
